newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 26.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The truth commission is to subpoena former African National Congress (ANC) activists and guerrillas involved in gross human righs violations including bombings, torture and murder, says commission investigations head Dumisa Ntsebeza.

- Anglogold, Anglo American's gold mining division, is to merge its low-cost Elandsrand mine with neighbouring Deelkraal, operated by Gold Fields of SA. The merger is seen by Anglo as a first step towards exploiting the major gold resource known as Western Ultra Deep Levels.

- Government would inject $1 billion of the proceeds of Telkom's 30 percent equity stake sale into the delivery of at least 1.8 million lines to previously disadvantaged areas, Deputy President Thabo Mbeki announced on Tuesday.

- Thirteen Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) supporters were convicted in the Durban High Court on Tuesday on charges of murdering and attempting to murder African National Congress (ANC) supporters in Shobashobane on the KwaZulu Natal south coast on Christmas Day 1995.

- Almost 2,000 police weapons went missing last year for reasons which included robberies and thefts, being left in toilets or shebeens, or being lost in the post, Safety and Security Minister Sydney Mufamadi said on Tuesday.
BUSINESS REPORT
- The role and duties of the life assurance ombudsman should be urgently re-examined, Judge Jan Steyn, the oubudsman for life assurance, said on Tuesday.

- More than 4.4 billion rand from Telkom's estimated 5.5 billion rand strategic equity deal with Telkom Malaysia and SBC Communications would be ploughed back into the state-controlled telecommunications company for infrastructural expansion, Thabo Mkeki, the deputy president, said on Tuesday.

- South Africans may soon be able to invest in sports companies, courtesy of a British fund manager run by former South Africans, Gideon Nurich, a marketing manager for Momentum International, said on Tuesday.

- Anglo American's Elandsrand is to buy Gold Fields of SA's Deekraal mine in a 420 million rand share swap deal that reflects a further rationalisation of mineral rights among South African gold mines, the companies said on Tuesday.
SAKE BEELD
- The government will inject 4.4 billion rand from the sale of 30 percent of Telkom into expanind telephone infrastructure, president Thabo Mbeki announced on Tuesday.
- Deelkraal and Elandsrand gold mines nearby Carletonville are going to merge.
THE STAR

- Anti-corruption and secret service units are to be introduced in prisons as part of the government's plans to rid the system of corruption, stem the tide of escapes and transform the Department of Correctional Services.
- A survey showing that most rape suspects walk free after their day in court has left women's groups shocked and with little faith in the criminal justice system.
- Inkatha Freedom Party leader and Home Affairs Minister Chief Mangosuthu Buthelezi has joined the ranks of leading politicians who have had their offical houses ransacked.
- A Johannesburg woman and her son were killed by three men in the industrial area of Alrode in Alberton on Tuesday.
